items.title: Treatment Discontinuation of Blood Pressure–Lowering Drugs—Reply
items.summary: In Reply We thank Dr Wu and colleagues for their interest in our article. The random-effects model demonstrated consistent results—this was a prespecified sensitivity analysis and can be found in eFigure 12 in Supplement 1 of the article. The overall point estimates and the uncertainty intervals were largely unchanged with random-effects compared with fixed-effects models. We chose to use fixed-effects models as the primary analysis because of the errors random-effects models are prone to, with potential undue influence of small studies.

items.title: Regional anaesthesia and chronic postsurgical pain: no low-income countries in the evidence base. Comment on Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 838–48
items.summary: Taylor-Rowan and colleagues1 synthesised 158 randomised trials and 18 794 participants to show that regional anaesthesia reduces the incidence of chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) for up to 12 months after surgery. For those of us who care for women after mastectomy, the subgroup estimate for single-injection regional blocks is the most consequential figure in the paper: a risk ratio (RR) of 0.68 (95% CI 0.59–0.78) for CPSP. It is the clearest signal yet on a question ranked among the top research priorities identified by an international Delphi study of anaesthetists.

items.title: Delayed gastric emptying in adolescent patients on glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists with standard preoperative fasting guidelines: separate drug effects from disease effects. Comment on Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 1507–13
items.summary: I read with interest the prospective cohort study by O'Brien and colleagues,1 which provides valuable gastric ultrasound data in adolescents taking glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1-RAs), a population for whom perioperative data remain scarce. That most participants had residual gastric solids despite a median 13 h fast is important, as current multisociety guidance addresses primarily adults.2,3 I do not question that GLP1-RAs can increase residual gastric contents; my concern is whether these data can establish a drug-specific effect.
